Spatial checks run on this data
Mangrove 2023, whole study area: raster-grid area vs exact polygon area (UTM)7215 ha vs 7170 ha (+0.63%)
Whole-area series vs Earth Engine table (all 40 years)max abs difference 1.23%, mean +1.21%
Last-year-present: my 15 m grid vs Earth Engine 30 m raster (points where either is mangrove)90.5% identical year, 91.4% agree on presence
Gain-year: my grid vs Earth Engine raster, points where either has a gain25% agree a gain exists; where both do, 72% differ by 2 years or less (154 points). Totals: 212 ha here vs 186 ha in the Earth Engine table
NDVI-anomaly overlay (20 m, averaged) vs source raster, colour bin at 6,000 mangrove pixels98.4% within one bin, 78.6% identical
Presence PNG pixel count 2023 vs rasterised polygons321161 px; PNG decodes to the same array by construction (tested in the browser run)
Found while checkingProtected_Areas (the six gazetted areas) does not intersect the study area at all; the county plan's "Mangroves" conservation zone covers 56% of the study-area mangrove, so that is the layer used.
Pixel-level gain and lossGain and loss are thin fringe changes in annual 30 m maps. Totals agree between my grid and the Earth Engine table (212 vs 186 ha gained, 135 vs 137 ha lost); individual pixel locations and years do not, so the dashboard states this and reports totals.
Whole-area extent7,215 ha in 2023 here versus 7,128 ha in the earlier summary: the earlier figure came from a vector intersection; the 1.2% gap is consistent in every year, so trends are unaffected.
Not testable offlineAlignment against live basemap tiles. Overlays use the same Web Mercator grid as the tiles; registration against the source rasters is tested above. Check the port marker against OSM when you open the file.
Validation: what loss and gain are78% to 79% of loss and gain pixels lie within 45 m of the persistent 2023 mangrove edge, which is why the dashboard calls them thin edge changes in 30 m maps and reports totals.
Validation: greenness flags27.6 ha is flagged by the 2026 greenness drop, but 44% of flagged pixels sit within 20 m of the mangrove edge against 11% of all mangrove pixels (4.1 times more often), so single pixels are noisy. The 64 patches of 0.1 ha or more total 15.8 ha, and 92% of them reach more than 20 m inside the mangrove; the headline uses those patches.
Validation: greenness baselineThe 2026 change has median +0.004 and standard deviation 0.039 across mangrove pixels, so there is no regional shift. Per-year greenness maps were not in the data, so a leave-one-year-out false-alarm rate could not be measured.

Mangrove extent: Continuous Global Mangrove Dynamics (CGMD) annual maps, 30 m, 1984 to 2023, drawn here at 15 m. Loss means the last mapped year was before 2023; gain means the first mapped year was after 1984. Degraded mangrove still counts as mangrove in this dataset, so loss understates dieback; the 2026 NDVI layer (Sentinel-2, January to September median against 2017 to 2022) is the early-warning check and covers 2024 to 2026, which the extent maps do not. Flagged patches are candidates for field verification, not confirmed loss. Single flagged pixels are noisy (44% sit within 20 m of the mangrove edge, against 11% of all mangrove pixels), so the headline counts patches of 0.1 ha or more, 92% of which reach more than 20 m inside. "Conservation zone" is the county spatial plan designation; none of the study-area mangrove lies inside the six gazetted protected areas.
